```plato

    // One vertex per edge; one face per original face plus one per original vertex.
    Ambo(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
                self.UndirectedEdgeMidpoints,
                Concatenate(
                    self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => self.AmboFaceOfFace(f)),
                    self.VertexCount.MapRange(v => self.AmboFaceOfVertex(VertexIndex(v)))));

    //==
    // Truncate — cut each vertex off a third of the way along its edges, so
    // every original n-gon becomes a 2n-gon and every vertex becomes a face of
    // its own degree (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truncation_(geometry)).
    // Cube -> truncated cube, icosahedron -> truncated icosahedron.

    // One new vertex per corner, a third of the way along that corner's edge.
    // The corner numbering therefore IS the truncated mesh's vertex numbering.
    TruncationPoints(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<Point3D>
        => self.CornerCount.MapRange(c => self.CornerLerp(CornerIndex(c), 1.0 / 3.0));

    // The widened copy of an original face: each of its edges contributes two
    // new vertices — the near one from the corner itself, the far one from that
    // corner's twin, which cuts at the other end of the same edge.
    TruncateFaceOfFace(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Array<VertexIndex>
        => (self.FaceArity(face) * 2).MapRange(k =>
            k % 2 == 0
                ? VertexIndex(self.FaceCorner(face, k / 2).Value)
                : VertexIndex(self.TwinCorner(self.FaceCorner(face, k / 2)).Value));

    // The face exposed by cutting a vertex off: the new vertex on each edge
    // that met there, in reversed rotation order so it winds counter-clockwise
    // seen from outside.
    TruncateFaceOfVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, vertex: VertexIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
        => self.ReversedVertexCornerRing(vertex).Map(c => VertexIndex(c.Value));

    // One vertex per corner; one face per original face plus one per original vertex.
    Truncate(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
                self.TruncationPoints,
                Concatenate(
                    self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => self.TruncateFaceOfFace(f)),
                    self.VertexCount.MapRange(v => self.TruncateFaceOfVertex(VertexIndex(v)))));

    //==
    // # Expand, snub and bevel on polygon meshes
    //
    // The three remaining Conway operators
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_polyhedron_notation) the catalog needs:
    // with them every Archimedean solid is a one-line program over a Platonic seed,
    // and every Catalan its dual (see the catalog sections above).
    //
    // Expand and snub share one construction: every FACE is shrunk toward its
    // centroid (and for snub also twisted about its normal), so the new vertex
    // numbering is the CORNER numbering of `meshes-polygon.library.plato`, exactly
    // as in truncate. The moved faces are then stitched back together:
    //
    //   expand    one QUAD per edge                       (the pulled-apart edge)
    //   snub      two TRIANGLES per edge                  (the quad, split with a twist)
    //   bevel     truncate of ambo (the Conway identity b = ta), nothing new
    //
    // plus one face per original vertex in both cases (the reversed vertex ring,
    // shared with truncate). Preconditions as for the other operators: a closed
    // manifold mesh with convex faces. The `shrink` and `twist` parameters are free;
    // the values that make the result UNIFORM (all edges equal) depend on the seed
    // and are recorded at the call sites in the expanded catalog above.
    // Snub is chiral: the twist sign picks the enantiomer, and the triangle split
    // below matches a POSITIVE (counter-clockwise seen from outside) twist.
    //
    // Like the core Conway operators above, nothing here
    // normalizes the result onto the unit sphere.

    //==
    // The shared vertex placement: one new vertex per corner.

    // A corner's vertex pulled toward its face's centroid by `shrink` (1 keeps
    // it in place, 0 collapses the face) and rotated by `twist` about the face's
    // outward normal, staying in the face plane. The in-plane rotation is
    // u * cos + (n x u) * sin for offset u and unit normal n.
    TwistedCornerPoint(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex, shrink: Number, twist: Angle): Point3D
    {
        var face = self.CornerFace(corner).Value;
        var centroid = self.FaceCentroid(face);
        var normal = self.FaceUnitNormal(face);
        var offset = centroid.Between(self.CornerPosition(corner)) * shrink;
        return (centroid.PositionVector
            + offset * twist.Cos
            + normal.Cross(offset) * twist.Sin).ToPoint;
    }

    // Every corner's moved vertex, in corner order: the vertex table shared by
    // expand and snub. The corner numbering therefore IS the result's vertex
    // numbering, and no lookup table is built.
    TwistedFacePoints(self: PolygonMesh3D, shrink: Number, twist: Angle): Array<Point3D>
        => self.CornerCount.MapRange(c => self.TwistedCornerPoint(CornerIndex(c), shrink, twist));

    //==
    // The moved copies of the original faces and vertices. The face copy is the
    // identity on corner numbers; the vertex face is truncate's
    // (`TruncateFaceOfVertex`), reused as-is since both name one new vertex per
    // corner of the ring.

    // The shrunk (and possibly twisted) copy of an original face: its own
    // corners, read as vertices of the result.
    MovedFaceOfFace(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Array<VertexIndex>
        => self.FaceArity(face).MapRange(slot =>
            VertexIndex(self.FaceCorner(face, slot).Value));

    //==
    // Stitching the pulled-apart edges back together.

    // The quad left where an edge was pulled apart: the edge's two corners on
    // one face and their twins' on the other, wound opposite to the moved faces
    // it borders so the result stays counter-clockwise seen from outside.
    // Precondition: `corner` is canonical (one call per undirected edge).
    ExpandFaceOfEdge(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
    {
        var twin = self.TwinCorner(corner);
        return [VertexIndex(self.NextCorner(corner).Value),
                VertexIndex(corner.Value),
                VertexIndex(self.NextCorner(twin).Value),
                VertexIndex(twin.Value)];
    }

    // The same quad split along the diagonal that matches a positive twist,
    // giving the snub's two edge-triangles.
    // Precondition: `corner` is canonical.
    SnubFacesOfEdge(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Array<Array<VertexIndex>>
    {
        var twin = self.TwinCorner(corner);
        return [[VertexIndex(self.NextCorner(corner).Value),
                 VertexIndex(corner.Value),
                 VertexIndex(twin.Value)],
                [VertexIndex(corner.Value),
                 VertexIndex(self.NextCorner(twin).Value),
                 VertexIndex(twin.Value)]];
    }

    // One stitch per undirected edge: folded over the corners keeping only the
    // canonical half of each twin pair, appending that edge's stitch faces.
    // `Repeat(0, ...)` is the empty seed.
    EdgeStitchFaces(self: PolygonMesh3D, stitch: Function2<PolygonMesh3D, CornerIndex, Array<Array<VertexIndex>>>): Array<Array<VertexIndex>>
        => self.CornerCount
            .MapRange(c => CornerIndex(c))
            .Reduce(Repeat(0, Repeat(0, VertexIndex(0))),
                (acc, c) => self.IsCanonicalCorner(c) ? Concatenate(acc, stitch(self, c)) : acc);

    // All faces of an expand or snub: the moved face copies, the vertex faces,
    // and the per-edge stitches.
    ExpansionFaces(self: PolygonMesh3D, stitch: Function2<PolygonMesh3D, CornerIndex, Array<Array<VertexIndex>>>): Array<Array<VertexIndex>>
        => Concatenate(
            Concatenate(
                self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => self.MovedFaceOfFace(f)),
                self.VertexCount.MapRange(v => self.TruncateFaceOfVertex(VertexIndex(v)))),
            self.EdgeStitchFaces(stitch));
```
